title: Segmented analytics sink mapper and residency enforcer
creator: Arielle Park
description:
Problem: Console usage events and token-level analytics are currently written into a single global stream and mirrored to regional analytics clusters via a generic fanout. Customers with strict data residency requirements need enforceable controls that guarantee analytics events never leave allowed regions, plus operational tools to inspect and remediate misroutes.

Goal: Implement a sink mapping and enforcement layer for the console analytics pipeline that: 1) computes per-tenant residency profiles, 2) maps events to one or more permitted regional sinks, 3) enforces routing policy at ingestion (accept/mask/drop/mirror-only), and 4) produces audit trails for every decision. The feature should support gradual rollout, a canary mode, and toggles for "masking" vs "deny remote" behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A resilient sink-mapper service exists that resolves tenant residency profile to an ordered list of permitted regional sinks within 50ms p95
Ingress components (sidecar or gateway) call sink-mapper and route events according to policy; misrouted events are not sent to unauthorized regions
Support three enforcement modes: allow_with_masking, mirror_only, deny_remote. Mode is configurable per-tenant and per-field (PII masking for email/phone fields)
All routing decisions are logged to an immutable audit stream with tenant id, residency profile id, decision, sink targets, and policy version
Automated test harness validates mapping for 100 synthetic tenants with mixed residency requirements and asserts zero events cross forbidden regions
Canary rollout plan defined and executed (start with 50 low-volume tenants, monitor metrics for 72 hours), and ability to rollback via feature flag
Metrics: replication_lag_p99, dropped_events_rate, unauthorized_routing_rate, mapper_errors, and cost_delta are available on dashboard and alert thresholds set
Design doc and schema for the sink-affinity table reviewed and approved by Security and PM
discussion: 2025-02-14 - Kickoff: Reviewed high-level approach with PM and Security. Agreement to implement centralized sink-mapper and keep enforcement at ingress for lowest blast radius.

2025-02-20 - Design review: Proposed sink-affinity table schema (tenant_id, residency_profile, allowed_regions, enforcement_mode, mask_policy, effective_from, version). Security asked to add 'legal_hold' flag per-tenant.

2025-02-25 - Engineering sync: Chose Kafka topics for audit stream (immutable, retained 7 years by default for enterprise tenants). Decided to use compacted topic for sink-affinity table replication across regions.
2025-02-28 - Spike results: Ingress sidecar -> sink-mapper latency added ~12ms p95 when colocated in same AZ. Fallback cache reduces p95 to ~6ms under steady load.
2025-03-01 - Security feedback: Require KMS-backed field-level encryption for any PII forwarded to non-home-region sinks even in mirror_only mode. Added 'mask_then_encrypt' flow to schema.
2025-03-03 - QA: Integration tests for masking policy failing intermittently under heavy load; investigating backpressure behavior in ingress component.
implementation_notes: Architecture: Implement sink-mapper as a small stateful service with a compacted Kafka changelog for the sink-affinity table so regional replicas can serve reads locally. Primary writes happen in control-plane region and are replicated asynchronously.

Enforcement: Ingress sidecars will consult a local cache first (TTL 30s) and fall back to sink-mapper. On cache miss, the ingress will apply conservative default (deny_remote) until mapper responds to avoid leakage.

Masking/encryption: Support pluggable field transforms. Default transforms: remove email domain, hash user_id, redact IPs. For 'encrypt' path, call KMS wrapper to perform envelope encryption and store encryption metadata in audit event.
Testing: Build a synthetic replay tool that replays production-sized event batches with tenant residency profiles to assert no forbidden cross-region writes.
Rollout: Feature flag per-tenant via console. Start with 'audit-only' where mapper logs would indicate violations but not enforce. Graduate to 'enforce' for canary tenants, then broad rollout.
Operational playbooks: Add runbook for 'mapper-unavailable' which prescribes switching affected tenants to audit-only and failing closed for high-compliance tenants.
Cost control: Provide telemetry on increased cross-region egress and extra mirroring storage so sales and CSMs can inform customers of opt-in costs.
